original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Panalytical, Worcestershire, UK) at 25 °C. The KDM4A tandem TUDOR domain (100 μM) was loaded into the sample cell, and the ligand (1a or 1b) was loaded into the syringe. The buffer used was 20 mM HEPES, pH 7.5, 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, 0.01% Tween-20. The ligand was titrated into the protein solution with 20 injections of 2 μL each, spaced 120 s apart. The stirring speed was set to 300 rpm. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA, USA) with a one-site binding model. The experiments were performed in triplicate, and the data are presented as mean ± standard deviation. The binding affinity (Kd) and stoichiometry (N) were calculated from the fitted curves. The KDM4B tandem TUDOR domain (916 to 1030 residues) was expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)-T1R and purified as described previously [30].

original_paragraph.Results section: Consistent with the X-ray crystallographic observations, ITC data presented in Fig. 4A and B shows that only 1a (not 1b) exhibits stoichiometric binding to the KDM4A-tandem TUDOR domain with a dissociation constant (Kd) of 81.7 ± 7.1 μM and competes with the H3(1–10)K4me3 peptide binding to KDM4A-TUDOR domain with an apparent Ki of 170 μM (Fig. S4, Table S1). Furthermore, mutating the three aromatic cage residues to alanine (F932A, W967A and Y973A) completely abrogates the binding of 1a to the KDM4A tandem TUDOR domain (See Fig. S5). These data further corroborate the binding mode observed in the X-ray structure (Fig. 3).

original_paragraph.Results section: To identify fragment binders to the KDM4A tandem-TUDOR domain we used 2D-NMR based fragment screening. This screening technique utilizing 15N or 13C-Heteronuclear Single Quantum Correlation (15N- or 13C-HSQC) spectroscopy, has been shown to be a very powerful tool in fragment based drug discovery. The tandem TUDOR domain present in KDM4A, 4B and 4C enzymes shares high overall sequence homology and a conserved aromatic cage constituting the tri-methylated lysine binding pocket (Fig. 1B). Purified tandem TUDOR domain from the KDM4A enzyme bound H3(1–10)-K4me3 and H4(16–25)-K20me3 peptides with similar affinities as measured by Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC) (See Fig. S1). We used 13C-labeled (only terminal methyl groups of the Ile, Leu, Val and Met residues) KDM4A tandem TUDOR domain protein (see Supplementary materials and methods section) to perform a 2D-NMR based fragment screen. As shown in Fig. 2A, comparison of the 13C-HSQC spectra of the protein itself (black) with that of the protein upon addition of H3(1–10)-K4me3 peptide (red) showed chemical shift perturbations (CSPs, indicated as Peak1 to 4 with arrows), which were used as indicators of binding. Using this we identified a total of six fragments from a library of ~3700 rule of three compliant fragments with a poor hit rate of less than 0.2%. Only fragment 1 [3-((dimethylamino)methyl)-1-phenylbicyclo[2.2.1]heptan-2-ol] (Fig. 2B) exhibit binding with a modest affinity of nearly 80 μM and showed CSPs of all the four major cross peaks (Peak1 to 4 in Fig. 2C) that were shifted upon H3(1–10)-K4me3 peptide binding, suggesting a competitive binding mode as desired for a functional antagonist. The other five fragments exhibit much weaker binding (affinities ranging from 0.5 to 1.5 mM as measured using 2D-NMR) and were not pursued further. In order to further understand the binding mode of fragment 1 to KDM4A TUDOR domain, we have solved the co-crystal structure of KDM4A-TUDOR domain in complex with 1 at 1.86 Å resolution.

51119125.DESCRIPTION: Binding affinity to thrombin cleavable N-terminal 6His tagged and 13C-IVLM labeled human KDM4A tandem TUDOR domain (897 to 1011 residues) expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)-T1R by ITC method
51119125.references_previous: 30. Shuker SB, Hajduk PJ, Meadows RP, Fesik SW. Discovering high-affinity ligands for proteins: SAR by NMR. Science. 1996;274:1531–1534.

original_paragraph.Materials and Methods: Isothermal Titration Calorimetry (ITC) experiments were performed on a MicroCal iTC200 instrument (Malvern Panalytical, Worcestershire, UK) at 25 °C. The KDM4A tandem TUDOR domain (897–1011) was expressed in Escherichia coli BL21(DE3)-T1R and purified as described previously [30]. The protein was labeled with 13C-IVLM (13C-labeled isoleucine, valine, leucine, and methionine) and thrombin cleavable N-terminal 6His tag. The protein was dialyzed against 20 mM HEPES (pH 7.5), 150 mM NaCl, 1 mM DTT, and 0.02% NaN3. The concentration of the protein was determined by UV absorbance at 280 nm using the extinction coefficient calculated from the amino acid sequence. The ligand 1a was dissolved in DMSO and diluted in the same buffer as the protein. The ITC experiments were performed by injecting 10 μL of the ligand solution (1.5 mM) into the sample cell containing 200 μL of the protein solution (0.15 mM) at 25 °C. The stirring speed was set to 750 rpm. The injections were spaced 120 s apart, and the duration of each injection was 10 s. The data were analyzed using Origin 7.0 software (OriginLab, Northampton, MA, USA) with a one-site binding model. The binding isotherm was fitted to the equation: Q = (n * ΔH * [L] * [P]) / (Kd + [L]), where Q is the heat of binding, n is the stoichiometry, ΔH is the enthalpy change, [L] is the ligand concentration, [P] is the protein concentration, and Kd is the dissociation constant. The control experiment was performed by injecting the ligand into the buffer without the protein. The data were corrected for the heat of dilution by subtracting the control experiment from the sample experiment.
